statement:
We want to let CLI users choose, per invocation, where a published event goes. Every CLI command that signs and publishes an event on the user's behalf (post, reply, react, delete, repost, profile-set, follow, unfollow, dm, nip-publish, attest and claim) should accept a repeatable `--relay <url>` flag. When one or more `--relay` values are given, the signed event must be sent directly to exactly those relays for that command, instead of the active identity's configured write relays / NIP-65 discovery. When the flag is absent, behaviour must stay exactly as it is today, and the MCP tools that expose the same operations must keep working without changes to their inputs. (publish-raw already supports this and is the model to follow.) There is one conflict: attest and claim already read a `--relay` value today and use it for a different purpose; that existing meaning must move to a new `--assertion-relay` flag so `--relay` can mean the publish target everywhere.

Before anyone writes code we need an impact analysis. Which source files and which functions or types must change, and what must change in each? Which other callers of the changed code are affected (including callers that need no edit but depend on the changed signatures), and do they need an edit? Do not modify any files; write your analysis to answer.json.
